title: Integration of body systems
summary: How nerves, hormones and the blood coordinate organs so the body works as one system, from reflex arcs to feedback control of heart and breathing rates, and (HL) how phytohormones coordinate plant growth.

keyterms.definition: A property of a whole system that arises from interactions between its parts and is not shown by the parts alone.
A neuron carrying impulses from receptors to the central nervous system (spinal cord or brain).
A neuron carrying impulses from the central nervous system to effectors such as muscles, stimulating contraction.
A bundle of nerve fibres of both sensory and motor neurons, surrounded by a protective sheath.
The pathway of a rapid involuntary response: receptor, sensory neuron, interneuron in the spinal cord, motor neuron, effector.
Part of the brain that coordinates skeletal muscle contraction and maintains balance.
A hormone secreted by the pineal gland, mainly in darkness, that modulates sleep patterns as part of circadian rhythms.
Adrenaline: a hormone secreted by the adrenal glands that prepares the body for vigorous activity, e.g. raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Part of the brain that links the nervous and endocrine systems, controlling the endocrine system via the pituitary gland.
A receptor in blood vessel walls that detects blood pressure; sends impulses to the medulla oblongata, which adjusts heart rate.
A receptor detecting chemical changes, e.g. blood pH, CO2 and O2 concentration; input is used to control heart rate and ventilation rate.
Waves of smooth muscle contraction that move food along the gut; involuntary and controlled by the enteric nervous system.
Directional growth of a plant shoot towards a source of lateral (one-sided) light.
A phytohormone that promotes cell elongation by acidifying cell walls; redistributed by auxin efflux carriers to produce phototropism.
A phytohormone produced in root tips and transported to shoots; interacts with auxin to regulate root and shoot growth.
A gaseous phytohormone that stimulates fruit ripening; ripening increases ethylene production, a positive feedback loop.

questions.prompt: Put the levels of organization in order, from smallest to largest.
items: Cells
Tissues
Organs
Organ systems
Organism
questions.explanation: Each level is a subsystem of the next; integration of these levels gives the organism properties that no single part has.

questions.prompt: A cheetah's ability to hunt effectively relies on its muscles, skeleton, nervous system and circulatory system working together. This ability is best described as:
options: a property of its muscle cells alone
a tissue
an emergent property of integrated body systems
a reflex arc
questions.explanation: Hunting success emerges only when many systems interact and are coordinated; no single organ or cell type can do it alone.

questions.statement: The spinal cord acts as an integrating centre for unconscious processes such as reflexes.
questions.explanation: Reflexes are processed in the spinal cord without needing the brain, which is why they are fast and involuntary; conscious processes are integrated in the brain.

questions.prompt: Match each structure to its role.

pairs.right: Carries impulses from receptors to the CNS
Carries impulses from the CNS to muscles
Links sensory and motor neurons in spinal grey matter
Bundle of sensory and motor fibres in a sheath

questions.explanation: Sensory neurons provide input to the spinal cord and brain, motor neurons carry output to muscles, and nerves carry both types of fibre together.

questions.prompt: Put the events in a pain withdrawal reflex in order.
items: Free nerve ending in the hand detects a painful stimulus
Sensory neuron carries the impulse to the spinal cord
Interneuron in the grey matter passes the impulse on
Motor neuron carries the impulse to the effector
Skeletal muscle contracts and the hand is pulled away
questions.explanation: The reflex arc passes through the spinal cord, not the brain, so the response is rapid and involuntary; the brain is informed afterwards.

questions.text: The ___ coordinates skeletal muscle contraction and balance.
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates the timing and strength of muscle contractions for smooth movement and balance; the medulla controls heart and ventilation rates.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the brain and spinal cord is correct?
options: All processing of sensory information happens in the spinal cord
Reflexes require a decision by the cerebral hemispheres
The brain does not receive any input from sensory neurons
Voluntary movements are initiated by the cerebral hemispheres, while reflexes are integrated in the spinal cord
questions.explanation: The brain is the central integration organ for conscious processes, learning and memory; output to muscles goes via motor neurons. Unconscious reflexes are integrated in the spinal cord.

questions.statement: In a pain reflex arc, the effector is smooth muscle.
questions.explanation: In a pain withdrawal reflex, the effector is a skeletal muscle (e.g. in the arm) that contracts to pull the hand away.

questions.text: Nerves contain fibres from both sensory neurons and ___ neurons.
questions.explanation: A nerve is a bundle of many nerve fibres, both sensory and motor, some myelinated and some not, enclosed in a protective sheath.

questions.prompt: Why is a pain withdrawal reflex so fast?
options: The impulse travels via the cerebral hemispheres
Only a few neurons and synapses are involved and no conscious decision is needed
Hormones carry the signal to the muscle
Pain receptors are myelinated, unlike all other receptors
questions.explanation: A short pathway through the spinal cord, with a single interneuron, minimises synaptic delays and bypasses conscious processing in the brain.

questions.prompt: Which statement about melatonin is correct?
options: It is secreted by the pineal gland, mostly at night, and promotes sleep
It is secreted by the adrenal glands during exercise
It is secreted by the pancreas after meals
It is secreted at a constant rate throughout the day
questions.explanation: Melatonin secretion rises in darkness and falls in light, helping to set circadian (daily) rhythms of sleep and wakefulness.

questions.statement: Melatonin secretion is highest during daylight hours.
questions.explanation: Light inhibits melatonin secretion; levels rise in the evening and are highest at night, promoting sleep.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT an effect of epinephrine in preparing the body for vigorous activity?
options: Increased heart rate
Increased breakdown of glycogen to glucose
Increased blood flow to the gut
Dilation of the airways
questions.explanation: Epinephrine diverts blood away from the gut towards skeletal muscles, while raising heart rate, blood glucose and airflow to support intense muscle contraction.

questions.text: The ___ links the nervous and endocrine systems and controls hormone secretion by the pituitary gland.
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus receives information from the nervous system and controls the pituitary gland, which in turn regulates many other endocrine glands.

questions.prompt: Match each structure to its role.

pairs.right: Detect blood pH and CO2 concentration
Coordinates changes in heart and ventilation rate

questions.explanation: Receptors send sensory input to the medulla, which sends nerve impulses to the heart or breathing muscles, forming feedback loops.

questions.prompt: Put the events in the feedback control of ventilation during exercise in order.
items: Respiration in muscles increases CO2 in the blood
Blood pH falls
Chemoreceptors detect the fall in pH
Impulses are sent to the respiratory centre in the brainstem
Impulses to the diaphragm and intercostal muscles increase ventilation rate
CO2 is removed faster and blood pH rises
questions.explanation: This is negative feedback: the response (faster ventilation) removes CO2, which reverses the change in blood pH.

questions.prompt: When baroreceptors detect a fall in blood pressure, what response does the medulla oblongata coordinate?
options: Heart rate decreases
Ventilation stops
Melatonin secretion increases
Heart rate increases
questions.explanation: Nerve impulses from the medulla to the sinoatrial node increase heart rate, raising blood pressure back towards normal (negative feedback).

questions.statement: Peristalsis is involuntary and is controlled mainly by the enteric nervous system.
questions.explanation: The enteric nervous system in the gut wall controls peristalsis; only swallowing and egestion are under voluntary control by the central nervous system.

questions.text: Swallowing and egestion are voluntary actions controlled by the ___ nervous system.
questions.explanation: The CNS controls the voluntary start (swallowing) and end (egestion) of the gut; the enteric nervous system controls peristalsis in between.

questions.prompt: How does the blood help integrate the organs of the body?
options: It carries nerve impulses between organs
It transports hormones, nutrients, oxygen, wastes and heat between organs
It produces all hormones
It coordinates muscle contraction directly
questions.explanation: Integration involves both signalling (nerves and hormones) and transport of materials and energy, which is done by the blood.

options: Growth of roots away from light
Directional growth of a shoot towards light coming from one side
Opening of stomata in light
Increase in photosynthesis rate with light intensity
questions.explanation: A tropism is a directional growth response to a directional stimulus; shoots grow towards lateral light, which helps maximise light absorption.

questions.prompt: Put the events of positive phototropism in a shoot in order.
items: Light falls on the shoot from one side
Auxin efflux carriers move auxin towards the shaded side
Auxin concentration becomes higher on the shaded side
Cells on the shaded side elongate more
The shoot bends towards the light
questions.explanation: Repositioning of auxin efflux carriers creates a concentration gradient; greater elongation on the shaded side causes curvature towards the light.

questions.text: Auxin causes H+ ions to be pumped into the cell wall; the low pH loosens cross-links between ___ fibres, allowing the cell to elongate.
questions.explanation: Acidification of the wall loosens connections between cellulose microfibrils, so turgor pressure can stretch the cell.

questions.statement: Auxin moves from cell to cell in one direction because auxin efflux carriers are positioned on one side of each cell.
questions.explanation: Coordinated positioning of efflux carriers in the plasma membranes of adjacent cells pumps auxin in a particular direction, creating and maintaining gradients.

questions.prompt: How do auxin and cytokinin interact to regulate root and shoot growth?
options: Root tips produce cytokinin that travels to shoots, and shoot tips produce auxin that travels to roots
Both are produced only in leaves
Auxin and cytokinin are the same hormone
Cytokinin is produced in shoot tips and inhibits root growth only
questions.explanation: Each hormone is transported to the other end of the plant, so the balance between them coordinates root and shoot growth.

questions.prompt: Match each phytohormone or protein to its role.

pairs.right: Made in root tips, transported to shoots
Gaseous hormone that stimulates fruit ripening
Membrane protein that pumps auxin out of cells

questions.explanation: Phytohormones are signalling chemicals controlling growth, development and responses to stimuli; efflux carriers maintain auxin gradients.

questions.statement: The relationship between fruit ripening and ethylene production is an example of negative feedback.
questions.explanation: It is positive feedback: ethylene stimulates ripening, and ripening fruit produce more ethylene, which speeds ripening further.

questions.prompt: What is the advantage of positive feedback in fruit ripening?
options: It delays ripening until winter
It keeps ripening slow and gradual
It causes rapid, synchronized ripening, attracting animals that disperse seeds
It prevents ethylene from spreading to other fruits
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gas that spreads between fruits, so ripening spreads quickly and fruits become ready together, making them attractive to seed dispersers at the same time.

questions.text: Signalling chemicals that control growth, development and responses in plants are called ___.
questions.explanation: Phytohormones such as auxin, cytokinin and ethylene act at low concentrations to coordinate plant growth and responses.

questions.prompt: How can a phototropic response in seedlings be measured quantitatively?
options: By counting leaves
By recording the colour of the shoot
By measuring root mass only
By measuring the angle of curvature of the shoot
questions.explanation: Tropisms can be recorded qualitatively with diagrams, or quantitatively by measuring the angle of curvature towards the light.
